metadata.title: Microservice reliability incident investigation
metadata.artifact_scope_note: Evidence is aggregated query output over a 24-minute telemetry capture (not raw samples or log lines); it contains no chat/communication records.

incident_description: Reliability incident investigation of the Online Boutique microservice application on a Kubernetes (GKE) cluster. Evidence consists of aggregated query output over Prometheus container metrics (CPU, memory, disk I/O, sockets, workload, error rate, latency p50/p90), application logs and Jaeger trace statistics. No root cause, impact or trigger is stated; these must be established from the supplied artifacts. Environment context: services: adservice, cartservice, checkoutservice, currencyservice, emailservice, frontend, paymentservice, productcatalogservice, recommendationservice, redis, shippingservice; services call each other over gRPC; frontend is the user entry point; redis is the cart store.
investigation_questions: What is the name of the service where the failure originated (the root-cause service)?
What is the name of the Kubernetes pod of the root-cause service?
On which Kubernetes node did the pod of the root-cause service run?
What type of fault caused the incident: CPU, memory, disk, network delay, packet loss, or socket?
Which of the three CIA components is primarily affected: availability, integrity, or confidentiality?
During what minute did the first signs of the failure appear? Provide the earliest date and time in YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM UTC format.
Which metric of the root-cause service best shows the fault? Give it as <service>_<indicator>, for example cartservice_cpu.
According to the trace latency statistics, which single service operation showed the largest latency increase? Is its service the root cause or a downstream symptom?
